title: Failure of local quasi-finiteness over a field produces a specialization
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $f$ is not locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], there exist distinct points $x,x^{\prime}\in X$ with $x^{\prime}\in\overline{\{x\}}$. Here $\overline{\{x\}}$ is closure in the Zariski topology, so this says that $x\leadsto x^{\prime}$ is a nontrivial specialization. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), contrapositive of (3) implies (1) over a field.

proof.text: Argue contrapositively. Suppose there are no distinct points $a,b\in X$ with $b\in\overline{\{a\}}$. For every $a$, the inclusion $\{a\}\subseteq\overline{\{a\}}$ and the assumption give $\overline{\{a\}}=\{a\}$, so every singleton is closed. Moreover, for any $x$ and $a$, the condition $x\in\overline{\{a\}}$ implies $a=x$. Thus every point is closed and has no distinct generalization.

source.place: Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), implication (3) to (1), contraposed over a field.

proof.text: Let $s$ be the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the projection $X_s\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(\{s\})=X$. Fix any $x\in X$ and view it in $X_s$ using this homeomorphism. Step 1 says that $\{x\}$ is closed in $X_s$ and that any $a\in X_s$ with $x\in\overline{\{a\}}$ equals $x$. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-fibre-point-quasifinite-criterion] to $g=f$, $Y=X$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $y=x$. Its locally-of-finite-type hypothesis is the hypothesis on $f$; its two fibre hypotheses were just checked. It follows that $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$.

source.place: Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), implication (3) to (1), contraposed over a field.

proof.text: Since $x$ in step 2 was arbitrary, $f$ is quasi-finite at every point of $X$. By the definition of locally quasi-finite in [pqf-def-quasifinite], $f$ is locally quasi-finite. This proves the contrapositive and hence the assertion. If $X$ is empty, the same universal statement is vacuous, so the antecedent of the original implication cannot hold.
